documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
TCM visit. No records from the hospital yet; history from patient, wife and his discharge instructions sheet.

12/30: vomited a large volume of blood at home, wife drove him to the ED. Fluids, an urgent scope that showed bleeding esophageal varices - banded. Admitted, home 1/2. The sheet says GI follow-up for banding in about 3-4 weeks; no new medications listed.

Before this he had a few weeks of being more tired and filling up fast at meals.

Since home: no more blood, stools brown, appetite fair, tired. No confusion. Sober since 6/24 - six months now, still in his program. AUDIT-C 0.

Meds: propranolol 20 BID, lactulose 30 mL BID, spironolactone 100, furosemide 40, pantoprazole 40, amlodipine 5.

Exam: BP 110/70, HR 66. Wt 76. Pale conjunctivae. Anicteric. Spider angiomas. Abdomen soft, mild flank dullness, nontender. No asterixis.

A/P
1. Bleeding esophageal varices, s/p endoscopic banding 12/30. Continue propranolol; GI banding series to continue - he has 1/27.
2. Anemia from blood loss - CBC today.
3. Cirrhosis with ascites, HE - regimen unchanged.
4. AUD - six months sober. Real progress despite the bleed.
5. Records requested from the hospital.

RTC 6-8 weeks; ED for any blood.

documents.title: Post-bleed labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Scott, your hemoglobin is 9.4 after the bleed (12.2 in August), platelets 78, INR 1.4, bilirubin 2.2. Kidneys fine. The blood count should climb back over the next weeks; we will recheck at your next visit. Call right away for black stools, vomiting blood, or lightheadedness.

documents.title: Emergency department record (visit 2025-12-30)
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT - PHYSICIAN RECORD
Date of visit: 12/30/2025

CC: vomiting blood.

HPI: 55-year-old man with alcohol-related cirrhosis and known esophageal varices, brought in by his wife after a large-volume hematemesis at home this afternoon. Over the past several weeks he has felt progressively more fatigued, gets full early, and has had mild, intermittent abdominal discomfort. Prior admissions for ascites and hepatic encephalopathy.

PMH: alcoholic cirrhosis with portal hypertension; esophageal varices with prior band ligation; hypertension; peptic ulcer disease; recurrent hepatic encephalopathy; recurrent ascites; alcohol use disorder.
Meds: amlodipine 5 mg daily, propranolol 20 mg BID, lactulose 30 mL BID, pantoprazole 40 mg daily, spironolactone 100 mg daily, furosemide 40 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
Social: former smoker, 20 pack-years. Alcohol use disorder, abstinent about 6 months, in an outpatient rehabilitation program. On disability, formerly a construction laborer.
FH: father with alcohol-related cirrhosis, died at 58; mother with hypertension and diabetes; sibling with alcohol use disorder.

Exam: Pale and diaphoretic. Abdomen distended with shifting dullness. Multiple spider angiomas across the chest. 

Labs: anemia and thrombocytopenia (see laboratory record).

ED course: Two large-bore IVs; crystalloid resuscitation with improvement. GI consulted. Bedside upper endoscopy after resuscitation: dilated veins of the distal esophagus with stigmata of recent hemorrhage; band ligation performed.

Impression: Acute variceal hemorrhage from esophageal varices due to portal hypertension.

Disposition: Admitted to the medical service with GI following.

reports.text:
ULTRASOUND ABDOMEN, LIVER SURVEILLANCE
Indication: Cirrhosis, HCC surveillance.
Comparison: 08/05/2025.
Liver: Nodular cirrhotic morphology, no focal lesion.
Portal vein: Patent, hepatopetal flow.
Gallbladder: Unremarkable.
Bile ducts: Not dilated.
Spleen: Enlarged, 15.0 cm.
Kidneys: Unremarkable.
Ascites: Small volume in the right upper quadrant and pelvis.
reports.conclusion: Cirrhosis without focal lesion. Splenomegaly. Small ascites.

documents.title: Ultrasound result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: No mass. Small fluid, similar to a year ago. Next surveillance in August.

documents.title: GI office call
documents.author: MA
documents.body: GI office scheduler called to confirm our fax number for his file. Per scheduler: banding done 1/27, next session tomorrow 2/24, another planned in early April. Procedure notes will be faxed "when signed." Noted for PCP.

reports.text: Sinus bradycardia, rate 48. Normal axis. PR, QRS and QT intervals normal. No ST or T wave changes.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
F/u cirrhosis, post-bleed.

Banding 1/27 and 2/24 per patient and GI scheduler; next in April. No further bleeding. Energy slowly better. Sober nearly 9 months. No confusion.

Pulse 48 on intake, rechecked manually 48, regular. He feels fine at rest, no fainting. On propranolol 20 BID unchanged since 2024.

Exam: BP 112/70, HR 48 regular. Wt 75.5. Anicteric. Abdomen soft, small flank dullness. No edema. No asterixis.

ECG today: sinus bradycardia 48, no block, intervals normal.

A/P
1. Bradycardia on propranolol. GI started it; calling them today before stopping - message left with the hepatologist covering.
2. Varices s/p bleed, banding ongoing.
3. Anemia - recheck today, expect improvement.
4. Cirrhosis with small ascites, HE history - unchanged regimen.

Will call him once GI weighs in.

documents.title: Propranolol - GI discussion
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Spoke with his GI physician. Agree with stopping propranolol given HR 48; they will lean on banding to finish eradication and will discuss other options if he bleeds again. Called pt: stop propranolol starting today. Removed from med list; pharmacy notified to cancel refills. Labs from yesterday: Hgb 10.8 (up from 9.4), platelets 80, bilirubin 2.3, albumin 2.9, INR 1.5. Told him the blood count is coming back.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Video Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video visit, he is at home with his wife; consent for video confirmed.

Off propranolol since March. Home cuff: pulses in the 70s, pressures around 110s/70. Banding session 4/7 done, GI said the veins are "smaller"; no letter here yet. No bleeding, no black stools. Lactulose 2-3 BMs. No confusion. Weight steady on home scale. Sober 10.5 months, still in group twice a week.

A/P: Stable. Continue lactulose, spironolactone, furosemide, pantoprazole, amlodipine. Labs and visit in July; surveillance ultrasound due August. ED for any bleeding.

documents.title: Hospital discharge summary (admitted 2026-06-30, discharged 2026-07-08)
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL - DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted via ED 06/30/2026   Discharged 07/08/2026
Services: Medical ICU; Hepatology; Interventional Radiology

Principal diagnosis: Acute esophageal variceal hemorrhage with hypovolemic shock.
Secondary: Decompensated alcohol-related cirrhosis with tense ascites and jaundice; portal hypertension; splenomegaly; thrombocytopenia; history of recurrent hepatic encephalopathy; hypertension; peptic ulcer disease; alcohol use disorder in sustained remission.

Presentation: Abrupt hematemesis at home with signs of hypovolemic shock on arrival. Background of jaundice, prior admissions for hepatic encephalopathy and upper GI bleeding. Endoscopic band ligation had failed to control his recurrent bleeding, and his nonselective beta-blocker had been discontinued because of bradycardia. On exam: tense ascites, scleral icterus, spider angiomata.

Home medications on admission (from prior records): amlodipine 5 mg daily, propranolol 20 mg BID, lactulose 30 mL BID, pantoprazole 40 mg daily, spironolactone 100 mg daily, furosemide 40 mg daily. Propranolol confirmed stopped in 03/2026; not resumed.

Labs: thrombocytopenia, elevated INR and low albumin.
Imaging: Abdominal ultrasound - shrunken liver, dilated portal vein, splenomegaly.

Hospital course: Resuscitated in the ED and admitted to the ICU. Packed red cells transfused. Octreotide infusion started for variceal hemorrhage. After stabilization, surgery and hepatology reviewed portosystemic shunt options for portal decompression; the consensus was a transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt. Therapeutic paracentesis for tense ascites. TIPS placed by interventional radiology on 07/02/2026 via right internal jugular access without complication. No rebleeding after TIPS. Octreotide completed. Mental status monitored closely after TIPS; lactulose continued. Ambulating at discharge.

Discharge medications: lactulose 30 mL BID (titrate to 2-3 soft stools); spironolactone 100 mg daily; furosemide 40 mg daily; pantoprazole 40 mg daily; amlodipine 5 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.

Follow-up:
1. PCP within 1-2 weeks.
2. Post-TIPS duplex ultrasound in about 3 weeks (scheduled).
3. Referral to the liver transplant center for evaluation; decompensated cirrhosis with more than 12 months of abstinence documented by his treatment program will be needed.
4. Return for bleeding, confusion, fever or abdominal pain.

documents.title: Liver transplant center intake (visit 2026-08-18)
documents.author: transplant hepatology
documents.body:
LIVER TRANSPLANT PROGRAM - INITIAL EVALUATION VISIT
Date of service: 08/18/2026

Dear colleague,

We met Mr. Pomeroy, 55, and his wife today for an intake visit. He has alcohol-associated cirrhosis decompensated by recurrent ascites, recurrent hepatic encephalopathy and variceal hemorrhage, most recently a bleed with shock in late June treated with a TIPS on 07/02. He reports abstinence since late June 2025 with ongoing participation in an outpatient program, and a former smoking history of 20 pack-years with none since 2023.

We reviewed the hospital records, your notes and the post-TIPS ultrasound.

Assessment: Appropriate to begin formal transplant evaluation.

Plan:
1. Our coordinator will schedule the evaluation testing and consultations at the center.
2. Please continue to support his recovery; we will request a letter from his treatment program and will monitor abstinence as part of evaluation.
3. Continue his current medications and your routine primary care.

We will keep you informed.

Transplant Hepatology
